battle.name: 金與遼的戰爭
battle.brief: 遼天慶八年（1114）夏，女真完顏部首領完顏阿骨打舉兵於寧州，集兵二千五百人，連破寧州與曉古倫；同年冬寧元之戰，金軍以孤軍破遼師號稱七萬之眾，斬首萬餘級，遼之東北藩籬盡裂。翌年正月建國號大金，此役遂開金遼百戰。卡面希臘火不在此戰場，當時的燃燒手段只有火矢、火油櫃與焚林。

kit.name: 希臘火
kit.history: 配在銅管裡的燃燒劑。配方是帝國的機密，配方和船一起沉了。

countries: 金與遼的戰爭開打時，兩個交戰方都還沒有完全成形。一方是女真完顏部聯合周邊女真、渤海部眾的起兵聯盟；另一方是契丹人建立、已統治北方一百六十餘年的遼朝。金方以完顏阿骨打為盟主，編制沿用女真舊俗：部落聯盟以「部」為單位，部有首領稱「孛堇」，大首領稱「都勃孛堇」，其下按「猛安」「謀克」編隊，約五百人為一猛安、百人為一謀克，謀克既是百人長的名稱，也是最小的作戰單位。起兵初期金軍自稱義兵，規模極小，靠漁獵部眾自備的皮甲、弓矢、馬匹湊集，沒有營壘，也沒有攻城器械。遼方的指揮系統是北面官與南面官並行：契丹本族的樞密院與諸路招討司掌軍政，漢人南面官署掌民政與漕運，東北防務由上京、中京兩路調兵，契丹精騎充當主力，漢兵與渤海兵充當步卒。寧元之戰時，遼軍在天祚帝與樞密院調集之下自中京、上京方向西來，號稱七萬。金國在1115年正月建國之後，才把這套部落編制升格為軍國制度，設軍師府與都統府分統諸路；1114年的金軍仍只是一支以義兵名義活動的部落聯盟。宋與西夏在整場戰爭中站在局外觀望，直到1122年宋徽宗趁遼亡之際北伐燕京，才把這場東北方的戰爭變成自己的戰爭。
countriesEn: When the Jin–Liao War broke out, neither of the two belligerents had yet fully consolidated itself. On one side stood a rising league of the Jurchen Wanyan clan together with the neighbouring Jurchen and Bohai communities who answered the call; on the other stood the Liao dynasty founded by the Khitan, which had already ruled the north for more than a hundred and sixty years. The Jin side took Wanyan Aguda as its leader and kept the old Jurchen organisation: the league was composed of clans, each clan had a chief called a bojin, the greatest of them a dubojin, and below them the men were arranged in meng'an and mouke, roughly five hundred men to a meng'an and a hundred to a mouke, a mouke being both the name of the hundred-man commander and of the smallest unit of combat. At the outset the Jin troops called themselves volunteers. They were very few, they came together out of a population of hunters and fishers with their own leather armour, bows and horses, and they had no camp works and no siege engines. The Liao command system ran the northern offices and the southern offices side by side: the Privy Council and the circuits of the Khitan themselves handled military affairs, the Chinese southern offices handled civil administration and the transport of grain, and the defence of the north-east drew troops from the Supreme Capital and the Central Capital, with Khitan cavalry as the spear and Chinese and Bohai soldiers as infantry. At Ningyuan the Liao army came west under the emperor and the Privy Council and was claimed to number seventy thousand. Only after the state was founded in the first month of 1115 was this tribal structure raised into a system of war and state, with a Directorate of Military Affairs and a Directorate of Commanders holding the several lines; in 1114 the Jin army was still a tribal league operating in the name of volunteers. The Song and the Western Xia stood outside the war as spectators, and it was only in 1122, when Emperor Huizong of the Song struck north at Yanying on the strength of the Liao's collapse, that this war in the north-east became a war of the Song's own.
people: 完顏阿骨打，即位後改名完顏旻，是女真完顏部都勃孛堇完顏烏雅乃的長子。烏雅乃在1113年已因不堪遼朝的索取而舉兵，事敗病故，阿骨打收拾舊部，於遼天慶八年（1114）在寧州聚眾起事，起兵時能號召的義兵為二千五百人。寧元之戰中他自將這支部隊，據林候敵而不輕動，等到遼軍鋒銳耗盡才發。完顏賏是他的弟弟，起義時隨軍作戰，寧元之戰率一千七百名敢死士繞到遼軍之後突陣，中流矢重傷，其後傷發而卒，《金史》記其年四十一。遼方的主事者是皇帝天祚帝耶律延禧，他在此戰之前已因朝政混亂、皇族與妃嬪爭權而大失人心，寧元敗後退保黃龍府，又走避於邊外，最終在1120年被金軍擒獲，遼朝此後又撐了五年才亡。遼朝經營東北的另一批重要人物是契丹諸部首領與燕京的漢人官員：前者多被金軍的行動裹挾而各自求存，後者在1122年宋軍攻破燕京時大批投降，成為金朝接管漢地的重要骨幹。雙方的下層則是大量被徵發、被擄掠與被強行編入隊伍的兵卒：金軍的義兵自備兵械，遼軍的漢兵與渤海兵多由州縣徵發，兩軍都靠冬季就地取糧與牛馬馱運維持，後勤的鬆散是這場戰鬥中遼軍崩潰的重要內在原因。
peopleEn: Wanyan Aguda, later renamed Wanyan Min, was the eldest son of Wanyan Uya'na, the dubojin of the Jurchen Wanyan clan. Uya'na had already risen in revolt in 1113 because he could not bear the Liao court's exactions; his rising was defeated and he died of illness, and Aguda gathered the old remnants of his followers and raised a force at Ningzhou in the eighth year of the Liao emperor's Tianqing (1114), calling up a body of volunteers said to number two thousand five hundred. At Ningyuan he led that body himself, holding his ground in the timber and waiting for the enemy, and only struck once the Liao's edge had been spent. Wanyan Sheng was his younger brother and fought with the insurgents from the start; at Ningyuan he led seventeen hundred men who would not retreat round to the rear of the Liao army and struck there, was hit by an arrow and badly wounded, and died afterwards of the wound, the History of Jin recording his age as forty-one. On the Liao side the man in charge was the emperor Tianzuo, Yelü Yanxi, who before this war had already lost much of the support of the court through disordered government and the quarrels of the imperial clan with the empress's party; after the defeat at Ningyuan he fell back on Huanglong prefecture and then withdrew beyond the frontier, and was finally taken by the Jin in 1120, the Liao surviving another five years before it fell. Another body of important figures in the Liao's north-eastern administration were the Khitan clan chiefs and the Chinese officials of Yanying: the former were swept along by the Jin advance and each looked to his own survival, while the latter surrendered in large numbers when the Song took Yanying in 1122 and became the backbone of the Jin takeover of the Chinese lands. Below both commanders stood the rank and file of the war, men levied, taken captive and forced into the ranks: the Jin volunteers brought their own weapons, while the Chinese and Bohai soldiers of the Liao were raised circuit by circuit from the prefectures and counties, and both armies lived on grain taken on the spot in winter and on what oxen and horses could carry. That looseness of supply was one of the internal reasons for the collapse of the Liao army in this engagement.
kits: 卡面這件兵器在此役中並不存在，而它本身就是值得寫下的理由。希臘火是拜占庭帝國自七世紀以來壟斷的燃燒劑：配在銅管之中，靠人力泵壓噴出點火的燃油，配方屬於帝國最高機密，配方與施放用的船只一同沉入海底。整個地中海與波斯灣的海戰記錄裡都有它，卻沒有一份遼代或金代文獻提到過它。1114年的東北亞戰場上，最接近希臘火位置的東西是火矢與火油櫃：火矢把浸過油的麻絮或布纏在箭鏃上，射擊時留下火種，遼與宋都用過；火油櫃則是盛著猛火油、以唧筒拋射的器械，唐末五代已見於攻城記載，遼承襲了這一套技術，《宋史》在太平興國四年（979）太原之役記遼軍以火油焚燒宋人攻城器械，字句雖有出入，仍可見火油櫃已是遼軍可以調用的成裝備。1114年之前的東北亞還沒有爆炸性火器，火藥武器要到十二世紀下半才成熟，所以寧元之戰的燃燒手段止於油、火與人為放火。真正的火出現在那一天：十一月的松花江下游草木乾枯，完顏賏率一千七百敢死士繞擊遼軍後方時，攜帶火種與乾草是合理的做法，殘存記載沒有明文，但遼軍號稱七萬人紮營在林草之間，一旦火起便無從收束。除去火的部分，兩軍的裝備仍有世代差距：金軍是女真皮甲、短複合弓、長柄槍與大量戰馬，遼軍則有柳葉式札甲與更完整的馬政，遼的騎兵在開闊地仍然老練，卻在森林與濕地之中展不開；攻城器械方面，金軍到1114年底仍然沒有砲與雲梯，所有勝負都靠騎兵機動與集中突擊決定。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card did not exist in this campaign, and that fact is itself the reason it is worth writing down. Greek fire was an incendiary monopolised by the Byzantine Empire from the seventh century onward: it was carried in bronze tubes, projected by pumping pressure as a burning fuel, its formula was the highest secret of the empire, and the formula and the ships that served it went down together into the sea. It appears in the naval records of the Mediterranean and the Persian Gulf, and not one Liao or Jin document mentions it. What stood closest to the place Greek fire occupied in the north-eastern Asian battlefield of 1114 were the fire-arrow and the fire-oil chest. The fire-arrow wrapped tow or cloth soaked in oil round the head of the shaft so that it left a burning brand where it struck, and both the Liao and the Song used it. The fire-oil chest was a vessel of naphtha thrown by a pump, it appears in siege accounts from the end of the Tang and the Five Dynasties, and the Liao inherited the technique: the History of the Song, in the account of the Taiyuan campaign of the fourth year of Taiping Xingguo (979), has the Liao army burning the Song's siege works with fire-oil, and although the wording is not entirely consistent it shows that the fire-oil chest was a standing piece of equipment the Liao army could call on. Before 1114 the north-east of Asia had no explosive gunpowder weapons; those matured only in the second half of the twelfth century, so the burning at Ningyuan went no further than oil, fire and fire set by hand. The real fire came on that one day: in the eleventh month the grass and timber below the Songhua River were dry, and when Wanyan Sheng led his seventeen hundred men round to the rear of the Liao army it is reasonable to assume they carried brands and dry grass with them; the surviving record does not say so in so many words, but with seventy thousand Liao men claimed to be encamped among woods and grass, fire once started could not be gathered in. Setting the fire aside, there was a generational gap between the equipment of the two armies: the Jin had Jurchen leather armour, short composite bows, long spears and a great many horses, while the Liao had leaf-shaped lamellar armour and a more complete horse system, their cavalry still experienced in the open country but unable to deploy in forest and marsh. In the matter of siege engines the Jin army still had neither bombards nor scaling ladders at the end of 1114; every result was decided by cavalry manoeuvre and by concentrated attack.
tactics: 起兵的第一階段，金軍用的是女真部落的傳統打法：不打大城，不列大陣，只挑遼朝邊防最薄的點，以小隊夜行晝伏，攻破一處便散回山林。寧州與曉古倫都是這樣拿下來的，小城無深溝高壘，守軍不多，一旦被突破即潰散，義兵得手後照例掠取皮帛、馬匹、器械而去。這也解釋了為什麼1114年的金軍雖然連破數城，卻仍舊不敢向中京方向推進。寧元之戰是雙方第一次正面較量，其部署可以看出金軍的用兵重心在集中而不在多：阿骨打以二千五百人據守樹林與高阜，不與遼軍先鋒接戰，等到遼軍鋒芒已竭、陣形散亂，完顏賏才以一千七百名敢死士繞到敵陣側後發動衝擊，使遼軍首尾不能相顧；主力隨即全線反擊，遼軍大潰，金軍追至斡里只寨並攻破其營柵。整場戰鬥裡，遼軍的問題是典型的以眾擊寡反而失控：兵多將少、號令不統一，契丹騎兵在林木草澤之間無法展開衝鋒，糧秣靠從上京、中京遠道輸送，冬季草場不足，士卒在寒氣中久候而銳氣盡失；遼軍也嘗試分兵應戰，先鋒與大隊之間的間隔被金軍抓住。追擊階段金軍同樣不留餘地，一路由寧元追到斡里只寨，再收掃周邊寨柵，奪馬、驅畜、收繳器械，作為冬季牧養與來春再舉的資本。1115年之後戰法轉趨系統化：金軍分五路進攻，各路設都統，奪地之後立即置官吏、籍戶口、括馬匹、分屯田，把佔領區變成可以自養的根據地，這一點與遼朝倚賴南面官府徵發的體制截然不同，也正是後來金能在十年內吃掉遼的原因。
tacticsEn: In the first stage the Jin army fought in the traditional manner of the Jurchen clans: it did not attack great cities and did not deploy in great arrays, but picked the thinnest points of the Liao frontier, moved in small bodies by night and lay up by day, and scattered back into the hills as soon as a place was taken. Ningzhou and Xiaogulun were taken in this way: these were small towns without deep ditches or tall walls, their garrisons were few, and once a breach was made they dissolved; the volunteers took leather, cloth, horses and weapons as was the custom, and left. This also explains why the Jin army, though it had carried several towns in succession during 1114, still did not dare advance towards the Central Capital. The battle of Ningyuan was the first direct meeting of the two sides, and its dispositions show that the Jin weight lay in concentration rather than in numbers: Aguda held two thousand five hundred men in the timber and on rising ground, gave no battle to the Liao vanguard, and waited until the Liao edge was spent and their order broken before Wanyan Sheng took seventeen hundred men who would not retreat round to the flank and rear of the enemy and struck, so that the Liao could not look to front or rear; the main body then attacked all along the line, the Liao host broke, and the Jin pursued them to the fort of Wolizhi and carried its barricades. The Liao's problem was the classic failure of a large army in the hands of a small one: too many men and too few commanders, orders that did not run, Khitan cavalry unable to deploy a charge among trees and marsh, and grain drawn by long haul from the Supreme Capital and the Central Capital, when the winter pastures were short and the men had stood in the cold until their spirit was gone. The Liao also tried to fight in separate bodies, and the gap between their vanguard and their main body is what the Jin took advantage of. The pursuit was carried through with the same thoroughness: the Jin ran from Ningyuan to Wolizhi, swept the surrounding stockades, took horses, drove off the herds and collected the weapons, all of it so much capital for wintering the horses and for the next spring's advance. After 1115 the method became systematic: the Jin advanced in five lines, each with its own commander, and as soon as ground was taken they appointed officials, registered the households, seized the horses and divided the land into garrison farms, turning the occupied country into a base that could feed itself. That was a very different thing from the Liao system, which depended on levies raised by the southern Chinese offices, and it was the reason the Jin could swallow the Liao within ten years.
data: 可核對的數字大致如下。時間：遼天慶八年（1114）夏，阿骨打在寧州起兵；同年先取寧州，再破曉古倫；冬，寧元之戰；翌年（1115）正月，金國於會寧府建立，國號大金，都會寧府，建元天輔；1115年內取黃龍府；1118年進克中京；1120年上京臨潢府陷落，天祚帝出走被擒；1125年遼亡。兵力：金軍起兵義兵共二千五百人，其中完顏賏率敢死士一千七百人；寧元之戰金軍投入的仍只是這支部隊，遼軍則記載為七萬人——這個數字顯然是遼方公文或事後追述的誇大之辭，實際參戰當在數萬之數，可信的部分是金軍以數千對數萬。戰果：《金史》記寧元一戰，遼軍死者萬餘級，生擒及虜獲數千，奪馬數千匹（另有記載作二萬匹者，當亦誇大），金軍乘勝追至斡里只寨並攻破其營柵。損失：金軍陣亡數目不見記載，完顏賏中流矢重傷，數年後因傷卒。距離：寧州（今黑龍江寧安、海林一帶）至寧元（今呼蘭縣西、松花江與嫩江合流附近）為數百里，騎兵一日可及；追擊至斡里只寨又數十里。物資：女真以漁獵與馬牛為資，起義時的兵械多為自備；遼軍冬季需自上京、中京輸送草料與糧食，路遠而塞。金國建立後行牛具稅、括馬與軍屯，屯田所得充軍實。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked run roughly as follows. In time: in the summer of the eighth year of Tianqing (1114) Aguda raised his force at Ningzhou; in the same year he took Ningzhou and then broke Xiaogulun; in the winter came the battle of Ningyuan; in the first month of the following year (1115) the state of Jin was established at Huining prefecture, the country was named Great Jin, the capital was Huining, and the era was called Tianfu; within 1115 Huanglong prefecture was taken; in 1118 the Central Capital was carried; in 1120 the Supreme Capital at Linhuang fell, the Liao emperor fled and was taken; the Liao ended in 1125. In strength: the Jin volunteers numbered two thousand five hundred in all, of whom Wanyan Sheng led seventeen hundred as his death-squad; at Ningyuan the Jin committed nothing more than that body, while the Liao army is recorded as seventy thousand strong — a figure that is plainly an exaggeration of Liao official writing or of a later reconstruction, the real strength engaged being some tens of thousands, and the part worth believing being that the Jin met tens of thousands with a few thousand. In results: the History of Jin records for the battle of Ningyuan that more than ten thousand of the Liao were killed, several thousand were taken alive or captured, and several thousand horses were taken (there is also a record of twenty thousand, likewise an exaggeration); the Jin followed up the victory to the fort of Wolizhi and carried its barricades. In losses: the Jin dead are not recorded, though Wanyan Sheng was hit by an arrow and badly wounded and died of the wound some years later. In distance: from Ningzhou (about Ning'an and Hailin in Heilongjiang today) to Ningyuan (west of the county of Hulan, near the meeting of the Songhua and Nen rivers) is some hundreds of li, a day's ride for cavalry; the pursuit to Wolizhi was a further several tens of li. In stores: the Jurchen lived by hunting, fishing and their horses and cattle, and the weapons with which they rose were largely their own; the Liao army in winter had to draw fodder and grain from the Supreme Capital and the Central Capital over long, blocked roads. After the state was founded the Jin levied an ox-unit tax, seized horses and established garrison farms, and the produce of those farms filled the army's supply.
cause: 金與遼的戰爭，起因是遼朝對女真部落的長期榨取與部族關係的破裂。遼立國百六十餘年，契丹人靠「以夷制夷」立國，把北方各族首領封為諸部官、將軍、宿衛，藉其控制廣漠草原，同時按年索取貂皮、銀兩、馬匹，名為貢物，實為常稅。女真完顏部所居的松花江上游本是渤海國故地，渤海人對遼的統治素懷不滿，1114年寧州一帶的渤海部眾多直接響應起兵。直接導火線是完顏部自身的反抗：完顏烏雅乃於1113年拒絕遼朝的索取而起兵，事敗病卒，其長子阿骨打收拾殘部，翌年在寧州再度聚眾，殺死地方官吏，據州城而自保。深層的原因則在體制：契丹皇族與妃嬪爭權、契丹貴族與漢人官署互相倚制，天祚帝在位時朝令屢變，北面官與南面官互不信任，東北防務的實際主持者既無權就地調動中京的精兵，也無力約束上京的諸部，阿骨打起兵之後，遼朝竟沒有一支能迅速平叛的部隊。更遠的背景是草原政權的更替本身：部落聯盟瓦解之後，契丹人靠漢地的官僚系統維持國家，而女真則在同一套邊疆制度下由附庸長成獨立的軍事力量，一場以二千五百人挑七萬之眾的起兵，就這樣把一個百年帝國的內在空虛暴露了出來。
causeEn: The Jin–Liao War grew out of the long squeeze the Liao court kept on the Jurchen clans and the breaking of the tribal relationship between them. The Liao had stood for more than a hundred and sixty years; the Khitan had founded the state on the principle of ruling one people through another, sealing the chiefs of the northern clans with titles of official, general and imperial guard so as to hold the wide grasslands through them, and at the same time taking from them every year furs, silver and horses under the name of tribute, which was in truth a standing tax. The upper Songhua, where the Jurchen Wanyan clan lived, had been the country of the old kingdom of Bohai, and the Bohai had long been ill content with Liao rule; in 1114 the Bohai communities about Ningzhou answered the rising in considerable numbers. The direct occasion was the resistance of the Wanyan clan itself: in 1113 Wanyan Uya'na rose because he refused the Liao's demands, his rising was defeated and he died of illness, and his eldest son Aguda gathered the remnants and in the following year massed men at Ningzhou, killed the local officials and held the town against the rest. The deeper cause lies in the structure of the state: the Khitan imperial clan and the empress's party quarrelled, Khitan nobles and Chinese offices held each other in a mutual dependence, and under Tianzuo the court's orders changed with the month. Those who actually directed the north-eastern defence had neither the authority to move the picked troops of the Central Capital on the spot nor the power to hold the tribes of the Supreme Capital in hand, and when Aguda rose there was not a single army the Liao could send quickly enough to put him down. A still deeper background is the plain fact of succession among the steppe polities: once the tribal league dissolved, the Khitan had held their state together by borrowing the bureaucratic machinery of the Chinese lands, while the Jurchen, under the very same frontier system, grew from a dependent into an independent military power. A rising of two thousand five hundred against a claimed seventy thousand laid bare the emptiness inside a state of a hundred years.
impact: 這場戰爭的直接後果，是遼朝在東北亞的整個藩籬在一個秋天裡垮掉，進而改變了亞洲大陸的權力格局。金軍先取黃龍府，再取中京與上京，天祚帝出奔被擒，1125年遼朝滅亡，契丹人西遷，在中亞建立西遼，把歐亞大陸的商路拉出一條新的走廊。對中原而言，代價同樣巨大：燕雲十六州與燕京、雲州等漢地要塞落入女真之手，1122年宋徽宗趁隙北伐燕京，卻在遼軍殘部與金軍夾擊下大敗，1125年以後宋金之間再無緩衝，三十年對峙之後便是靖康之難。對女真本身，這是一場制度生成的戰爭：金以猛安謀克為軍隊基幹，兵農合一，部落首領的部曲制被改造為可以調度全國兵力的編制，後來元的怯薛、漢軍與巡檢制都能在這套框架裡找到源頭；金初的牛具稅與軍屯，則是把戰利品轉化為國家財政的第一套辦法。對後世史家而言，此役還示範了一種以小擊大的典範：以二千五百人破號稱七萬之眾，靠的不是器械，而是集中、耐心與敢死式的側翼突擊，這在後來的金宋戰爭中一再重演。至於兵器，此役同樣是分水嶺：希臘火那樣由國家壟斷配方的燃燒武器壓根沒有踏進這個戰場，東亞的燃燒技術仍停在猛火油與火矢一級，爆炸性火器要等到十二世紀下半才出現，那時金人攻破汴京所用的火器已把城防的舊秩序徹底改寫——一百多年後，技術才追上了這場戰爭留下的啟示。
impactEn: The immediate consequence of this war was that the whole Liao bulwark in north-eastern Asia collapsed within a single autumn, and the balance of power on the continent changed with it. The Jin took Huanglong prefecture first, then the Central Capital and the Supreme Capital; the Liao emperor fled and was taken, the Liao dynasty ended in 1125, and the Khitan moved west to found the Western Liao in Central Asia, opening a new corridor along the trade routes of Eurasia. For the Chinese lands the price was just as heavy: the Sixteen Prefectures of Yanyun and the Chinese strongholds of Yanying and Yuzhou passed to the Jurchen; in 1122 Emperor Huizong of the Song struck north at Yanying on the strength of the moment and was badly beaten between the remnants of the Liao and the Jin; after 1125 there was no buffer left between Song and Jin, and after thirty years of standoff came the disaster of Jingkang. For the Jurchen themselves this was a war in which institutions were made: the meng'an and mouke became the backbone of the army, soldiers and farmers were one, and the old private following of a clan chief was converted into an organisation that could move the troops of the whole country, and the later Yuan institutions of keshig, Chinese army and patrol all trace back to that frame. The early Jin tax on the ox and its garrison farms were the first attempt to turn the spoils of war into the finance of a state. To later historians the campaign also set a model for how a small force beats a large one: two thousand five hundred men broke a host claimed at seventy thousand, and what did it was not the weapons but concentration, patience and a flank attack by men who did not intend to come back — a method that was repeated in the Jin–Song wars that followed. In arms as well, this campaign was a watershed. A burning weapon whose formula was monopolised by the state, like Greek fire, never set foot on this battlefield; the burning technology of eastern Asia remained at the level of naphtha and fire-arrows, and explosive gunpowder weapons did not arrive until the second half of the twelfth century, when the engines the Jin used to break Bianjing put an end for good to the old order of city defence. More than a hundred years later, technology caught up with the lesson this war left behind.
result: 寧元之戰的結果，是遼軍在東北的野戰主力當場瓦解：死者萬餘級，生擒及虜獲數千，奪馬數千匹，斡里只寨的營柵被攻破，遼軍退回黃龍府，寧州、曉古倫一帶的邊柵盡失，金軍在整個冬天控制了松花江下游。翌年正月阿骨打在會寧府即位，國號大金，都會寧府，建元天輔，義兵正式成為王朝的軍隊；同年取黃龍府，1118年進克中京，1120年上京臨潢府陷落、天祚帝出走被擒，1125年遼亡。但1114年這一年留下來的問題並沒有被解決：遼失的是地盤，金得的卻是尚未習慣統治漢地的部落軍隊，契丹的官僚系統、燕京的財賦與南面漢官的網絡仍在原地等待接替者；金人此時尚靠括馬、屯田與臨時的徵發維持戰爭，制度的缺口要到1123年太宗即位之後才被系統補上，而缺口之處正是此後金宋三十年的消耗戰。從兵器角度看，此役的結論同樣清楚：戰場上沒有希臘火，燃燒靠油製火矢、火油櫃與冬季乾草的人為焚燒，火藥武器尚未問世，攻城塔與砲也還沒有出現在金軍的裝備表上；真正決定勝負的是騎兵的機動、集中突擊、敢死式的側翼衝鋒，以及把戰場從平曠帶進森林時雙方對地形的適應差距。
resultEn: The result of the battle of Ningyuan was the immediate disintegration of the Liao field army in the north-east: more than ten thousand killed, several thousand taken alive or captured, several thousand horses taken, the barricades of the fort of Wolizhi carried, the Liao falling back on Huanglong prefecture, and the frontier stockades about Ningzhou and Xiaogulun lost, so that the Jin army held the lower Songhua for the whole of that winter. In the first month of the following year Aguda took the throne at Huining prefecture, named his state Great Jin, made Huining his capital and opened the Tianfu era, and the volunteers became in name what they had always been in practice, the army of a dynasty; in the same year Huanglong prefecture was taken, in 1118 the Central Capital was carried, in 1120 the Supreme Capital at Linhuang fell and the Liao emperor was taken in his flight, and the Liao ended in 1125. But the problems left over from 1114 were not solved by it: the Liao had lost its territory, and what the Jin had gained was a tribal army not yet used to ruling Chinese lands, while the Khitan bureaucratic system, the revenue of Yanying and the web of southern Chinese offices were still in place waiting for a successor. The Jin were still maintaining the war by seizing horses, opening garrison farms and making improvised levies, and the gap in their institutions was only filled systematically after Taizong took the throne in 1123 — and it was precisely that gap that made room for the thirty years of attrition between Jin and Song. As to arms, the conclusion of the campaign is equally plain: there was no Greek fire on the battlefield, the burning was done with oil-soaked fire-arrows, with fire-oil chests and with the deliberate firing of dry grass in winter; gunpowder weapons had not yet appeared, and siege towers and bombards were not yet on the Jin list of equipment. What really decided the outcome was the mobility of the cavalry, the concentrated attack, the flank charge by men who did not intend to retreat, and the difference between the two sides in how well they had adapted to a battlefield moved from open plain into forest.
